# Contributing

Thanks for looking. This project is alpha (`0.1.0aN`) and pre-1.0, so a bug
report with a reproduction, or a note on where the documentation misled you,
is the most useful thing you can bring right now.

How this project writes prose — README, `CHANGES`, `MIGRATION`, commit
messages, docstrings, and source comments — is set out separately in
[WRITING.md](WRITING.md). Read that before changing any of it. The constraints
every change is held to, and the map of what is where, are in
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).

## Getting set up

```console
$ uv sync --all-packages --group dev
```

This installs both workspace packages editable, plus docs, testing, and lint
tooling, from the single root lockfile.

## The gates

Format:

```console
$ uv run ruff format .
```

Lint:

```console
$ uv run ruff check .
```

Add `--fix --show-fixes` to apply ruff's safe fixes:

```console
$ uv run ruff check . --fix --show-fixes
```

Type-check:

```console
$ uv run ty check
```

This project uses [ty](https://docs.astral.sh/ty/), not mypy — there is no
mypy configuration or dependency here. `ty` consumes `django-stubs` as PEP 561
stubs and checks at the workspace's `py312` floor.

Test:

```console
$ uv run pytest
```

Documentation is a gate, not a courtesy. Doctests in both packages' `src/` and
in `docs/` are collected and run by this same `pytest` invocation — see
[Documented examples that run](WRITING.md#documented-examples-that-run) for
which blocks qualify and the one mistake that silently removes a test.

Before claiming a test or a gate works, show it failing. A gate that has
never been red is an assumption.

CI (`.github/workflows/tests.yml`) runs the same four checks — lint, format
check, type-check, test with coverage — across a matrix of Python 3.12/3.14
and Django 5.2/6.0/6.1. Passing locally on one interpreter is not the same
claim as passing CI.

## Coding standards

- Every Python file starts with `from __future__ import annotations`; ruff's
  `isort` `required-imports` rule enforces it.
- Prefer namespace imports for the standard library (`import typing as t`);
  third-party packages may use `from X import Y`.
- Type hints are required; `ty` checks the whole workspace, so an untyped
  public function fails the gate above rather than review.

## Tests

`DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=tests.settings` is set in `pyproject.toml`
(`pytest-django`, with `django_find_project = false`); the settings install
both workspace apps plus the admin and its supporting apps, so the admin
integration is exercised from the same run as the core package. Use
`pytest.mark.django_db` only when a test touches Django models — most tests
in `tests/` are pure functions against the parser and compiler.

The `e2e` marker (declared in `pyproject.toml`) is skipped by default —
`conftest.py` adds the skip unless the run explicitly selects `-m e2e`. The
end-to-end suite drives the colored admin search input through Playwright and
needs a browser installed:

```console
$ playwright install chromium
```

```console
$ DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=tests.settings_e2e uv run pytest -m e2e
```

`tests/test_search_endpoints.py` is the browser-free proof of the same
contract and always runs. `tests/test_lexer_parity.py` compares the Python
highlighter against its JavaScript port live when `node` is on `PATH`, and
otherwise falls back to a captured fixture that still pins the Python side.

```console
$ just start
```

runs the suite once, then keeps re-running it on file changes via
`pytest-watcher` (`uv run ptw .` directly, if you do not use `just`).

## Debugging

When stuck in a loop:

- Acknowledge the loop and list what has already failed.
- Minimize to the smallest reproducible case; drop debugging cruft before
  sharing it.
- Document the exact error and the current hypothesis.
- Share a portable repro block — code plus output — before iterating again.

## Documentation

```console
$ just build-docs
```

builds the single Sphinx site covering both packages
(`just -f docs/justfile html` under the hood). For live-reload while writing:

```console
$ just start-docs
```

Sphinx's own doctest builder is separate from `pytest` and only it reads
`docs/conf.py`'s `doctest_global_setup`:

```console
$ just -f docs/justfile doctest
```

A stricter, from-scratch build that turns warnings into errors and catches a
broken cross-reference:

```console
$ just -f docs/justfile checkbuild
```

`docs/_static/fonts/` and `docs/_static/css/fonts.css` are generated by the
build (gitignored) — do not hand-edit them.

## Releasing

Never create tags. Never push tags. The owner handles tagging and tag
pushes, because a tag triggers the publish workflow. See
[Release commits](WRITING.md#release-commits).

Each package is versioned and released independently: a release bumps one
package's version and records it in the shared root `CHANGES` and
`MIGRATION`, without touching the other package. The version lives in two
places per package — `packages/<name>/pyproject.toml`'s `[project].version`
and `packages/<name>/src/<module>/__about__.py`'s `__version__` — and both
must move together. See
[`docs/project/releasing.md`](../docs/project/releasing.md) for the full
process.

## Pull requests

One subject per pull request. Unrelated cleanup found along the way belongs
in its own commit, and usually in its own pull request.

Discuss a substantial change via an issue before making it.

Commit format is in [WRITING.md](WRITING.md#commits).

## Decorum

- Participants will be tolerant of opposing views.
- Participants must ensure that their language and actions are free of
  personal attacks and disparaging personal remarks.
- When interpreting the words and actions of others, participants should
  always assume good intentions.
- Behaviour which can be reasonably considered harassment will not be
  tolerated.

Based on [Ruby's Community Conduct Guideline](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/conduct/).

## Security

Please do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. There is no
`SECURITY.md` in this repository yet — open a private report through
[GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/tony/django-search-query/security/advisories/new)
instead.
